audience: New Yorkers comparing blocks before renting, buying or walking
the project owner and agents working on this repository
problem: Open NYC data on noise, crashes, housing complaints and street improvements is scattered across many Socrata datasets, so judging one block means opening several portals and reconciling different units.
solution: A browser map that aggregates registry-defined NYC datasets onto a block grid and shows per-source and average concern views with walking routes and street-level imagery.
mechanism: a dataset registry declares each source, its query and polarity
points are aggregated to a roughly 300 m block grid
per-source and average concern scores are rendered as map layers

evidence.claim: The map aggregates registry-defined NYC datasets onto a block grid.
evidence.supports: The registry file lists the datasets the map queries.
evidence.limits: Shows the datasets are wired, not that scores are accurate.

boundaries: not an official City of NYC product
scores summarize reported data and inherit its reporting bias

terminology.concern score: average of per-source normalized values with polarity
